dedupe_keys.name: usgs shakecast shakemap broadcast automated post earthquake facility impact estimates and inspection priority notifications

description: ShakeCast, short for ShakeMap Broadcast, is a USGS post-earthquake situational awareness application whose source is published on the USGS GitLab (code.usgs.gov). Contents: after an earthquake it automatically retrieves ShakeMap ground-motion values at a user's facilities, compares them with damage functions (Hazus-based, intensity-based or custom; building-specific Hazus AEBM functions since version 3 in the companion shakecast-aebm repository) and sends notifications with potential impacts and inspection priorities to emergency managers; facilities can be buildings, campuses, bridges or bridge components. pyCast is the current Python backend with an Angular web frontend and scenario tools. Producer: USGS (repository group ghsc/esi); the wiki cites Lin, Wald and Slosky (2020). Coverage: any region with USGS ShakeMaps; Caltrans has used it since 2005 and nine other state transportation departments joined a Transportation Pooled Fund from 2017. Format and access: open source code on code.usgs.gov with a wiki, an Excel Inventory Workbook that exports facilities, notification groups and users as XML, and cloud or on-premise deployment. Licence: CC0 1.0 (repository licence). Caveats: the wiki says ShakeCast needs a sizeable facility inventory and expertise in earthquake engineering and IT; results depend on the fragility assigned to each facility. Simulation uses: rapid damage and inspection prioritisation for bridge, utility and facility portfolios, and scenario exercises for emergency response planning. Related records: data-usgs-shakemap-scenario-catalog, data-fhwa-national-bridge-inventory and platform-hazus.
